text:
ajay: Heads-up, noticed sustained proxy queue growth in eu-west yesterday ~18:30. tail latencies spiked and fallback routing hammered dedicated pools.

tomas: saw that. pgpu1 nodes showing high dma_wait. logs have repeated `proxy: route fallback invoked` entries (x1200).

lina: is this the same tenant that warmed kvcache last week? their prefix churn looked noisy.

ajay: @sarah can you check slab counts and NIC q depth?

sarah: on it. pulled telemetry snapshot:
```
proxy: fallback_invocations=1200
kv_cache: regen_rate=0.9
nic0: txq_depth=512
```

infra-bot: Alert: dedicated-pool-eu-west CPU overload (SLA risk) — incident created #inc-17295

tomas: short term: flip routing weight to prefer dedicated for low-latency customers and rate-limit fallback. long term: reduce fallback fanout and add per-tenant backpressure.

lina: cost note: extra dedicated cycles will increase monthly committed usage. rough estimate +8% if we tilt routing for 6 hours.

ajay: proposed runbook: 1) throttle fallback via proxy config (`max_fanout=4`) 2) bump kv cache TTL for heavy tenants 3) schedule warmup prefill for affected tenants 4) open a canary to validate.

sarah: :thumbsup: I'll push the proxy change to canary eu-west-a and watch 15m.

deploy-bot: deploy started: proxy-config-change -> canary-eu-west-a by sarah (rev 245) — status: in-progress

sarah: canary showed ~40% drop in fallback invocations after 5m, tail latency down ~25ms. pushing to eu-west-b next.

ajay: nice. postmortem note: consider adding `fallback-slowstart` to avoid cascade when cold kvcache regen occurs; fallback should ramp not flood. follow-up ticket?

tomas: I'll file the ticket and include rollout plan + cost calc. tagging ops & infra for priority.

lina: :raised_hands: thanks — will update finance on commit budget impact and add a line to weekly infra sync.

ajay: summary action items: `proxy max_fanout` change merged to region, canary validated, ticket for slowstart, cost impact tracked. closing thread unless new regressions pop.
